subtopics.title: Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane

command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Laws of indices
kcs.statement: Laws of indices for all rational exponents.
kcs.raw: Laws of indices for all rational exponents.
kcs.guidance: $a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}$, $a^m \div a^n = a^{m-n}$, $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$. The equivalence of $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$ and $\sqrt[n]{a}$, and of $a^{\frac{m}{n}}$ and $(\sqrt[n]{a})^m$, should be known.

kcs.title: Manipulating surds
kcs.statement: Use and manipulation of surds.
kcs.raw: Use and manipulation of surds.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to rationalise denominators.

kcs.title: Quadratic functions and graphs
kcs.statement: Quadratic functions and their graphs.
kcs.raw: Quadratic functions and their graphs.

kcs.title: The discriminant
kcs.statement: The discriminant of a quadratic function.
kcs.raw: The discriminant of a quadratic function.
kcs.guidance: Need to know and to use $b^2-4ac>0$, $b^2-4ac=0$ and $b^2-4ac<0$.

kcs.title: Solving quadratic equations
kcs.statement: Completing the square. Solution of quadratic equations.
kcs.raw: Completing the square. Solution of quadratic equations.
kcs.guidance: Solution of quadratic equations by factorisation, use of the formula, use of a calculator and completing the square: $ax^2+bx+c = a\left(x+\dfrac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + c - \dfrac{b^2}{4a}$.

kcs.title: Simultaneous equations by substitution
kcs.statement: Solve simultaneous equations; analytical solution by substitution.
kcs.raw: Solve simultaneous equations; analytical solution by substitution.

kcs.title: Interpreting inequalities graphically
kcs.statement: Interpret linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
kcs.raw: Interpret linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
kcs.guidance: For example, $ax+b>cx+d$, $px^2+qx+r \geq 0$, $px^2+qx+r<ax+b$. Interpreting the third inequality as the range of $x$ for which the curve $y=px^2+qx+r$ is below the line with equation $y=ax+b$. Including inequalities with brackets and fractions; these are reducible to linear or quadratic inequalities, e.g. $\dfrac{a}{x}<b$ becomes $ax<bx^2$, $x \neq 0$.

kcs.title: Graphing inequality regions
kcs.statement: Represent linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
kcs.raw: Represent linear and quadratic inequalities graphically.
kcs.guidance: Represent linear and quadratic inequalities such as $y>x+r$ and $y>ax^2+bx+c$ graphically. Shading and use of dotted and solid line convention is required.

kcs.title: Solving linear and quadratic inequalities
kcs.statement: Solutions of linear and quadratic inequalities.
kcs.raw: Solutions of linear and quadratic inequalities.

kcs.title: Manipulating and factorising polynomials
kcs.statement: Algebraic manipulation of polynomials, including expanding brackets and collecting like terms, factorisation.
kcs.raw: Algebraic manipulation of polynomials, including expanding brackets and collecting like terms, factorisation.
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to expand brackets and collect like terms. Factorisation of polynomials of degree $n$, $n \leq 3$, e.g. $x^3+4x^2+3x$. The notation $f(x)$ may be used.

kcs.title: Sketching curves and using intersections
kcs.statement: Graphs of functions; sketching curves defined by simple equations. Geometrical interpretation of algebraic solution of equations. Use of intersection points of graphs of functions to solve equations.
kcs.raw: Graphs of functions; sketching curves defined by simple equations. Geometrical interpretation of algebraic solution of equations. Use of intersection points of graphs of functions to solve equations.
kcs.guidance: Functions to include simple cubic functions and the reciprocal functions $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$ and $y=\dfrac{k}{x^2}$ with $x \neq 0$. Knowledge of the term asymptote is expected. Also, trigonometric graphs.

kcs.title: Graph transformations
kcs.statement: Knowledge of the effect of simple transformations on the graph of $y=f(x)$ as represented by $y=af(x)$, $y=f(x)+a$, $y=f(x+a)$, $y=f(ax)$.
kcs.raw: Knowledge of the effect of simple transformations on the graph of y = f(x) as represented by y = af(x), y = f(x) + a, y = f(x + a), y = f(ax).
kcs.guidance: Students should be able to apply one of these transformations to any of the above functions (quadratics, cubics, reciprocals, sine, cosine, and tangent) and sketch the resulting graphs. Given the graph of any function $y=f(x)$, students should be able to sketch the graph resulting from one of these transformations.

kcs.title: Equations of straight lines
kcs.statement: Equation of a straight line, including the forms $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ and $ax+by+c=0$.
kcs.raw: Equation of a straight line, including the forms y − y1 = m(x − x1) and ax + by + c = 0.
kcs.guidance: To include: (i) the equation of a line through two given points; (ii) the equation of a line parallel (or perpendicular) to a given line through a given point. For example, the line perpendicular to the line $3x+4y=18$ through the point $(2,3)$ has equation $y-3=\dfrac{4}{3}(x-2)$.

kcs.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
kcs.statement: Conditions for two straight lines to be parallel or perpendicular to each other.
kcs.raw: Conditions for two straight lines to be parallel or perpendicular to each other.

kcs.title: Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area
kcs.statement: The sine and cosine rules, and the area of a triangle in the form $\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
kcs.raw: The sine and cosine rules, and the area of a triangle in the form 1 2 ab sin C.
kcs.guidance: Including the ambiguous case of the sine rule.

kcs.title: Radians, arc length and sector area
kcs.statement: Radian measure, including use for arc length and area of sector.
kcs.raw: Radian measure, including use for arc length and area of sector.

kcs.title: Trig function graphs and periodicity
kcs.statement: Sine, cosine and tangent functions. Their graphs, symmetries and periodicity.
kcs.raw: Sine, cosine and tangent functions. Their graphs, symmetries and periodicity.
kcs.guidance: Knowledge of graphs of curves with equations such as $y=3\sin x$, $y=\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $y=\sin 2x$ is expected.

kcs.title: Derivative as gradient and rate of change
kcs.statement: The derivative of $f(x)$ as the gradient of the tangent to the graph of $y=f(x)$ at a point; the gradient of the tangent as a limit; interpretation as a rate of change; second order derivatives.
kcs.raw: The derivative of f(x) as the gradient of the tangent to the graph of y = f(x) at a point; the gradient of the tangent as a limit; interpretation as a rate of change; second order derivatives.
kcs.guidance: For example, knowledge that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is the rate of change of $y$ with respect to $x$. Knowledge of the chain rule is not required. The notation $f'(x)$ and $f''(x)$ may be used.

kcs.title: Differentiating powers of x
kcs.statement: Differentiation of $x^n$, and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
kcs.raw: Differentiation of xn, and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
kcs.guidance: The ability to differentiate expressions such as $(2x+5)(x-1)$ and $\dfrac{2x^2+5x-3}{3x}$ is expected.

kcs.title: Tangents and normals
kcs.statement: Applications of differentiation to gradients, tangents and normals.
kcs.raw: Applications of differentiation to gradients, tangents and normals.
kcs.guidance: Use of differentiation to find equations of tangents and normals at specific points on a curve.

kcs.title: Integration as reverse of differentiation
kcs.statement: Indefinite integration as the reverse of differentiation.
kcs.raw: Indefinite integration as the reverse of differentiation.
kcs.guidance: Students should know that a constant of integration is required.

kcs.title: Integrating powers of x
kcs.statement: Integration of $x^n$ and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
kcs.raw: Integration of xn and related sums, differences and constant multiples.
kcs.guidance: (Excluding $n=-1$, and related sums, differences and multiples). For example, the ability to integrate expressions such as $(x+2)^2$ and $\dfrac{3x-1}{2x^2}$ is expected. Given $f'(x)$ and a point on the curve, students should be able to find an equation of the curve in the form $y=f(x)$.
